I wrote a throwaway test at /tmp/repro/repro.test.ts with its own vitest config and ran it against the repo at 8b6d008. No tracked files were changed. The test starts the real Fastify app via buildApp, loads a 30-slide deck with 5 open lanes, POSTs one accept, and records the bus events. It then replays the dispatch in Main.tsx:123-130: for deck.changed or any lane event it calls GET /api/lanes and then GET /api/lanes/:id/preview once per open lane. An onRequest hook counts the preview GETs.

Command: `cd /Users/sderosiaux/code/personal/deckstudio && npx vitest run --config /tmp/repro/vitest.config.ts --reporter=verbose`

Output:
```
DISJOINT events= ["deck.changed","lane.updated"] reloadLanes= 2 previewGETs= 10
ORPHANING events= ["deck.changed","lane.updated","lane.updated","lane.updated","lane.updated","lane.updated"] reloadLanes= 6 previewGETs= 30
Tests 2 passed (2)
```

The reviewer's worst case reproduces exactly: 6 reloadLanes × 5 lanes = 30 previews. That is O(L²).

Caveat: the claim that there is "one lane.updated per rebased lane" is only true for lanes that the rebase actually changes. LaneService.accept (laneService.ts:53) emits an event only when a lane's JSON differs after rebaseLane, which only happens when a change becomes an orphan. When lanes touch different slides, the accepted lane is the only one that emits, so you get 2 reloads and 2L previews, not L². The cost becomes quadratic when the accepted change orphans changes in other lanes, for example when it removes a slide they modify. My ORPHANING case has 4 other lanes that modify s1 while l1 removes s1.

The rest of the claim checks out in the code:
- Every preview runs inside store.withLock (laneService.ts:91), so an accept or an agent write queues behind the preview burst.
- The deck.changed handler already reloads every lane, so the lane.updated events that follow it only add work.
- laneGen (Main.tsx:56-66) only discards stale responses on the client. It does not cancel the work on the server.
confirmed.fix_hint: In Main.tsx onEvent: on lane.created/updated call refreshPreview(e.laneId) (plus getLanes for metadata), on lane.closed drop that lane from lanes/previews, and do the full reloadLanes() only on deck.changed (or debounce/coalesce reloadLanes to at most one in flight plus one queued).
